review_scope: Complete 158-line pinned article read; all 80 parsed candidates separately accounted in docs-ai-model-hosting-artifact.json. Provider statements are historical source declarations, not current legal advice or provider agreements verified for a target. Variables, time-bound exceptions, beta exclusions, plan scope, hosting/developer identity, caching, retention, no-training and user opt-outs remain distinct. Variable expansions, external terms/model cards, rendered branches and independent omission certification remain outstanding. No external license/terms clearance, adoption or live runtime assurance.

claims.statement: Model-hosting article scope depends on the Copilot feature declaration, not actual customer availability.
The OpenAI roster is expressed through thirteen variable references; resolve each at the pinned data source before assigning a concrete model.
The pinned OpenAI section names OpenAI and GitHub Azure as hosting infrastructure; no per-request host receipt is provided.
The page attributes a no-business-data-training commitment to OpenAI; linked terms require separate review and do not establish all-provider data handling.
The page states GitHub maintains an OpenAI zero-retention agreement; this is not proof that a target request used a qualifying endpoint.
Copilot inputs/outputs pass through filtering; public-code checks are conditional when applied, not universal match blocking.
The Anthropic roster uses eleven model variables whose concrete values/version scope require pinned resolution.
The page states named Fable models retain prompts and outputs by default for safety classifiers; general Claude ZDR cannot be inherited.
Fable ZDR is described as an eligible-enterprise, requested, approved and configured time-bound exemption through end2026.
The page describes continued Fable use after that exemption as requiring Enterprise Frontier Safeguards; expiry must trigger reassessment rather than indefinite grandfathering.
Fable exemption eligibility/access requests require the customer's GitHub account team; local agent authority cannot grant it.
Fable access approval does not enable the model; enterprise/organization administrators must separately enable each model.
Other Claude models are stated to retain ZDR except named Fable cases; beta/feature exceptions elsewhere in the page still apply.
Fable ZDR use is restricted to internal operations including customer-product development/evaluation.
Fable ZDR terms described in the pin prohibit making model endpoints or outputs externally available; no distribution approval follows from access.
Anthropic-family models may be hosted across AWS, Anthropic and Google Cloud; model developer and serving provider are separate identities.
Provider no-training agreements are described; no-training and retention are separate properties.
The page attributes no prompt/completion storage/logging, training or third-party distribution to Amazon Bedrock; actual applicable provider terms remain separately referenced.
Generally available Anthropic Copilot features have a described ZDR agreement, with named Fable models excluded by default.
Eligible Fable exemption ends in2026; eligibility and configuration must be evidenced, not presumed.
Some beta/public-preview Anthropic features, including Messages API tool search, are outside the described ZDR agreement and may retain data.
The page describes Google Cloud no-training and a GitHub exemption from abuse-monitoring prompt logs; neither certifies every Google deployment.
Claude serving uses prompt caching to improve latency/quality; cache policy needs separate review instead of equating no-training with no storage.
Claude Copilot traffic remains filtered, with public-code matching conditional on application.
The Gemini roster contains four model-variable references; these are not literal resolved model identities.
Gemini Copilot prompts and metadata are sent to Google Cloud; the page separately attributes a no-training commitment.
Gemini serving uses prompt caching; retention details are linked independently.
Gemini input/output filtering retains conditional public-code checks.
The xAI roster contains three unresolved model-variable references.
The page states xAI serves these models under a ZDR API policy; this is a pinned declaration, not runtime endpoint evidence.
Described xAI policy prohibits input/output logging, including human review.
Described xAI policy prohibits disk saving or retention, including metadata.
Described xAI policy prohibits xAI-personnel access to user content.
Described xAI policy prohibits model training on user content.
Described xAI content lifetime is transient RAM for minimum request processing.
Described xAI content deletion occurs from memory when response is delivered; actual deletion is not verified here.
xAI Copilot traffic remains filtered, with public-code matching conditional on application.
The named Microsoft model is first-party and hosted on Azure in GitHub's tenant; concrete model variable requires resolution.
The Microsoft section states Business/Enterprise customer data is not used by GitHub for AI training.
The Microsoft section permits training/improvement use for listed individual subscriptions subject to privacy terms and user settings; enterprise no-training cannot be generalized to individuals.
Listed individual subscribers may opt out of training use through a separate account-policy setting; no opt-out state is observed here.
Microsoft-model processing/retention/security depend on GitHub's Azure Foundry deployment configuration and linked provider guidance, not tenancy alone.
Microsoft-model Copilot traffic retains conditional public-code and harmful-content filtering.
Open-weight means publicly available weights; linked hosting reusable remains independently reviewed evidence, not a universal open-source license.
Named Moonshot models may have weaker alignment and elevated geographic bias; open weights are not safety certification.
The page instructs reviewing each model card before enabling either named Moonshot model.
The page instructs running customer-specific evaluations before enabling either named Moonshot model.
The first named Moonshot model is stated to be served on GitHub/Microsoft-managed Azure Foundry.
The second named Moonshot model is stated to be served by GitHub on Fireworks AI; developer identity does not identify host.
The Moonshot section describes ZDR agreements with hosting providers and no host training on prompts/completions.
The Moonshot section states prompts/completions are not sent to Moonshot AI; this is separate from GitHub's own data-use policy.
The Moonshot section states GitHub does not train on Business/Enterprise customer data.
The Moonshot section permits listed individual-subscription interaction data use subject to terms/settings, independently of host ZDR.
Individual opt-out controls are linked separately; no active opt-out is verified.
Named Moonshot-model traffic continues through Copilot filters; filtering does not prove license clearance or vulnerability absence.
Inline ghost-text/next-edit hosting is Azure for Business/Enterprise but Fireworks for Free/Student in the pin; interactive-model host claims do not exhaust inline service scope.
